key_insight: LIBERO-PeRM introduces a controlled benchmark that separates whether a robot completes a task from whether it matches a user’s preferences. This makes it possible to measure personalized robotic manipulation more precisely than standard manipulation benchmarks.
problem_solved: Existing robotic manipulation benchmarks focus mostly on task success and do not cleanly evaluate preference satisfaction in household-style settings. The paper addresses the lack of a standardized benchmark for studying personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) and preference learning in embodied agents.
method: Introduces LIBERO-PeRM, a benchmark designed to test preference-aware robotic manipulation in controlled environments.
Frames evaluation around preference satisfaction separately from task completion, enabling cleaner analysis of personalized behavior.
Organizes the benchmark around five research questions, including zero-shot preference following.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this benchmark provides a clearer way to evaluate and compare methods for personalized robotics. It can accelerate research on robots that adapt to human preferences in practical household settings.
